# Node.js Notes: NPM, package.json, and Dependencies

## Key Concepts
* **`package.json`**: A configuration file in the root directory that contains project metadata and tracks a general list of top-level dependencies.
* **`package-lock.json`**: Automatically generated by npm when a dependency is modified. It records the exact, precise version of every installed package and sub-dependency to guarantee matching environments across different machines. **Do not modify this file manually.**
* **`npm init`**: The terminal command used to launch an interactive prompt that automatically generates a standard `package.json` template.

---

## Final Project Structure
```text
Artster/
│
├── package.json        (Tracks general dependencies & version rules)
├── package-lock.json   (Locks down the exact, precise dependency tree)
├── index.js            (Main application entry point)
└── node_modules/       (Folder containing actual source code of libraries)
```

---

## 1. Project Configuration (package.json)
This file is generated by `npm init` and automatically updated by npm when running install commands.

```json
{
  "name": "artster",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "An ASCII art terminal application",
  "main": "index.js",
  "scripts": {
    "test": "echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1"
  },
  "author": "Instructor",
  "license": "ISC",
  "dependencies": {
    "colors": "^1.4.0",
    "figlet": "^1.5.0"
  }
}
```

---

## 2. Main Application File (index.js)
This script imports `figlet` to generate ASCII typography and the `colors` package to stylise the terminal output.

```javascript
const figlet = require("figlet");
const colors = require("colors");

// Generate ASCII art text
figlet('Hello World!!', function (err, data) {
    if (err) {
        console.log('Something went wrong...');
        console.dir(err);
        return;
    }
    // Print the ASCII art to the terminal in green text
    console.log(data.green);
});
```

---

## 3. Complete Command Line Workflow
```bash
# 1. Create a project directory and navigate into it
mkdir Artster
cd Artster

# 2. Initialize the package.json file (press Enter to accept defaults)
npm init

# 3. Install packages (This generates node_modules/ and package-lock.json)
npm i figlet
npm i colors

# 4. Run the application
node index.js
```
